status: Research input for round 39; not yet reviewed by a person; not wired into build_data.py.
what: Extra services sold to Ukraine (the services twin of sell_ukr): per exporting economy, services exports to Ukraine 2019-2026, the no-war expectation, the extra amount and the money flowing back it implies at the seller's net gain x genuinely extra. Two parts: (1) travel = Ukrainian money spent abroad by refugees and travellers (NBU card-based travel imports above the expected level, allocated by host); (2) non-travel = transport, ICT, business and other services, as the exporter reports them, without government goods and services (SL) and maintenance and repair (SB).
units: EUR bn current prices unless a key says _eur_m or _usd_m; 2026 = January-August, projected from the first half (NBU Q1-Q2 2026) as H1 2026 + 2/3 of Q3 2025 grown at the H1 growth; low/central/high ~90% range. Effect = gross extra x factor, summed 2022-Aug 2026.
years: 2019-2025 calendar years (2025: Eurostat/BaTiS have no partner-UA data yet, projected from 2024 with Ukraine's own imports of that kind, NBU); 2026 Jan-Aug projected

rules.no_war_expectation: The project's services rule (services-shipping-companies.md; counterfactual.md: '2021 held flat' for services and for trade with Ukraine): 2021 volume held flat at the euro-area services price level (energy2.json price_index.services, 2019-2021 = 1), plus, for travel only, the COVID shortfall of 2021 against 2019 closing at the UNWTO world pace (49% of the gap still open in 2022, 17% in 2023, 1% in 2024, 0 after). Range: non-travel between the 2019-2021 mean, 2021 and a damped 2017-2021 trend (3-year half-life, capped at +-10% a year), at the price index's low/high; travel between that rule and the 2019 level held.
rules.extra: actual - expected, each year, summed over 2022-Aug 2026 with their signs; only the weighted total is floored at zero (index.html above3(), the sell_ukr rule). Falls (e.g. fewer Ukrainian seasonal workers spending in Poland, less business with Türkiye) offset rises in the same country.

shares.travel: net_gain_sellers.json group refugee_spending (retail G47, accommodation and food I, rent without imputed rent; OECD median 0.047, Poland 0.161) x value_kept.json flowback_other.extra (0.25/0.45/0.65): the factors refugee_flowback() already applies to hosting money spent in the host's economy, since the same refugees spend it in the same shops
shares.nontravel: net_gain_sellers.json group services (accommodation and food I + business services without real estate GTNXL; OECD median 0.040, Poland 0.181, US 0.109) x value_kept.json services_to_russia.extra_when_more (default 0.30/0.50/0.70): the factors svc_sold uses when a country sells more
shares.combination: build_data.py _gain_x_extra(): independent errors in absolute terms

rules.allocation_of_travel: NBU personal travel above expected x refugee key (refugees.json UNHCR end-year counts x intensity: 1 in Europe, Germany 0.5, Moldova 0.6, outside Europe 0.5; Germany hosts ~20% of Ukrainian migrants but receives ~10% of Ukrainian card spending, VoxUkraine on NBU data); NBU business travel (short-term workers) shortfall x pre-war worker key (POL 0.60, CZE 0.12, ITA/DEU/SVK 0.04, HUN/LTU 0.03, ESP/PRT/ISR 0.02, 4% by refugee key; judgement D)

double_counting.refugee_hosting_flowback: refugee_flowback() applies to host GOVERNMENT spending (aid.refugee_back_f x hosting cost). The travel part here is only Ukrainian money: NBU's travel imports are card payments and cash withdrawals abroad on Ukrainian-issued cards. Host benefits are paid into host accounts and host wages are refugees' own income (and the host's gain on their work is already subtracted), so neither is in the central. Partner-recorded travel credits DO include host-financed spending where the host counted refugees as non-residents (Czechia Q1-Q3 2022: CZK 28bn+ above the 5-year average, then moved to resident consumption, CNB BoP Report 2022 fn 20), so they are used only to widen the range, never as central.
double_counting.goods_sell_ukr: sell_ukr is customs goods exports (FOB in the seller's own report). Travellers' purchases are not in customs; freight and port services on Ukrainian cargo are services, outside FOB values. Residual risk: card spending with foreign online merchants that ships goods to Ukraine (in customs postal/express imports, revised by NBU in 2026) - not separable.
double_counting.money_ledger: Excluded SL (government goods and services n.i.e.: embassies, military and donor-paid government services) and SB (maintenance and repair: repair of donated or bought weapons, in the ledger's 'weapons, new money: equipment, services'). US: BEA's total moves with security assistance (USD 1.1bn in 2021, 7.6/14.5/12.4bn in 2022-24) and is not used; only Ukraine's computer-services imports from the US (NBU table 2.4) count. Budget support spent by refugees on Ukrainian pensions abroad is in the ledger as 'spent in Ukraine' (no flowback), so counting it here once is not a double count.
double_counting.svc_sold_russia: partner UA only; uncovered.json services is partner RU. No overlap.
double_counting.remittances: personal transfers are not services; not included.

world.mirror_check: Ukraine's own non-travel imports without government and repair (NBU, EUR m): 5,987 in 2021; 5,845 / 6,698 / 8,326 / 9,165 in 2022-25; about 6,505 Jan-Aug 2026. Against 2021 held flat that is about EUR 5bn extra over 2022-Aug 2026, part of it the 2022 statistical break (digital services sold to individuals, added from tax data). The partners' non-travel extra summed with signs over all countries is EUR 2.7bn (positive parts 10.1bn, negative parts -7.4bn: France, Hungary, the UK, Lithuania, Switzerland and others sell less). The two sides agree on the order of magnitude. The partners' split between travel and the rest is modelled (BaTiS), so part of a host's 'non-travel' rise may be refugee spending: the low end of each non-travel extra is at most 0.45 x its central.
